title: Witness the capture dim in another tool on an unlocked screen
goal: The screen darkening that a region capture puts up is supposed to show up in screen recordings and shared screens from the first instant, and the code that makes it do that has shipped. Nobody has actually seen it happen yet, because the Mac was locked when it was built and a locked Mac photographs as the lock screen. Watch it work once on a real screen, so the fix is witnessed rather than argued.
notes:
Witnessed and closed on 2026-09-05. All four acceptance items pass on an unlocked screen.

To re-run:
  ioreg -n Root -d1 -a | plutil -extract IOConsoleLocked raw -   # must print false
  Scripts/build-app.sh --probe
  Scripts/probe-app.sh --quit; open -a "$PWD/dist/Photonz Probe.app" --args --capture-diag
  cat /tmp/photonz-capture-diag.txt
Note the ABSOLUTE path: `open -a "dist/Photonz Probe.app"` fails to resolve.

Result: overlay shareable at 38 ms, dim measurable in another tool at 112 ms, freeze lands at 169 ms. Resting on a window, 6% of the display washed to 0.762 of clean; mid drag, 87% washed to 0.750 with the box left clean. Frozen picture 1.000 of clean. Shadow 0.0373 through both capture paths, so 100% as deep as before: the SHADOW LOST fallback the old notes described is not needed, ignoreShadows = false did fix it.

THE TRAP, if this is ever re-run: do not judge the dim by mean luma over the display. Window picking opens the dim with a hole over the window under the pointer, so a large window leaves the display average almost unchanged (0.993 of clean) while the dim is present and correct. That misread reported a working feature as broken three runs in a row. CaptureDiag now uses dimCoverage(of:against:), which compares each shot against a clean shot cell by cell and reports the fraction washed and how dark, plus a control line that must read 0% once the overlay is gone.

Artifacts every run: /tmp/photonz-capture-diag-clean.png, -predrag.png (overlay up, before any pointer event) and -drag.png. Audit: queue/audits/2026-09-05-capture-dim-witnessed.json, which supersedes the unwitnessed parts of queue/audits/2026-09-03-capture-dim-in-recordings.json.
acceptance: The probe report at /tmp/photonz-capture-diag.txt says the screen was unlocked on its first line
Its dim line says the dim shows up in another tool screenshot, at about 0.75 of clean rather than 0.99
The frozen picture under the overlay measures the same brightness as the real screen, so the world is never dimmed twice
A window drop shadow inside a captured region still looks the way it did before the freeze changed capture APIs

Witnessed on an unlocked screen (IOConsoleLocked false before and after every run). All four acceptance items pass: line 1 says unlocked; the dim reaches another tool's screenshot 112 ms after the shortcut at 0.762 of clean; the frozen picture measures 1.000 of clean, so the world is never dimmed twice; the window shadow through the freeze path is 100% as deep as the old path (0.0373 both ways), which closes the one real risk the notes flagged.

The first three unlocked runs reported 'dim NEVER shows up ... 0.993 of clean', and that was the diagnostic lying, not the feature. It averaged luma over the whole display, but window picking opens the dim with a hole over the window under the pointer, and the pointer sat on a 1728x1027 window on a 1728x1117 screen. Proved it by mapping predrag against a clean shot on a 48x24 grid: only the menu bar row and the strip below the window were washed, everything else pixel-identical to clean, while the drag shot showed the whole screen washed except the box. Replaced the whole-screen mean with dimCoverage(of:against:), which compares against the clean shot cell by cell and reports what fraction is washed and how dark; a hole can no longer hide the dim. Added a control line (overlay gone must read 0% washed; it does), a clean PNG, and a predrag PNG taken before any pointer event. Also fixed a bug my own change introduced: the poll now breaks at ~110 ms, before the freeze lands at ~169 ms, so the freeze report is preceded by a wait rather than reporting 'no display froze one'.

Adversarial pass on the built thing: one honest UX finding, not fixed on purpose. When the pointer rests on a window that fills most of the screen, starting a capture washes only 6% of the display, so almost nothing visibly changes and it can read as 'nothing happened'. That is window picking working as designed (it previews what a click would capture) and the outline and size pill do appear, so whether a capture should announce itself more loudly is a product call. Put it in the audit's evaluate and rough so the user can react to it rather than guessing for them. Scripts/test.sh green (3225 tests). Probe quit. Audit with two real screen captures at queue/audits/2026-09-05-capture-dim-witnessed.json.
